THE EVERYDAY CHALLENGE

SensoryScout starts
with a real need.

A place described as quiet may be very different at another time. Useful sensory information needs context: who reported it, when they visited, and which conditions mattered to them.

Help people make informed plans using available information, personal preferences, and visible uncertainty.

HOW IT COULD WORK

A thoughtful path
through the moment.

This walkthrough illustrates the intended experience. It describes the product direction, not functionality available on this website.

  1. Describe what matters

    Set preferences for aspects such as noise, lighting, crowds, and break opportunities. Needs should be adjustable from one outing to the next.

  2. Review the available picture

    Compare reports and available environmental information. The intended experience would show source and freshness details rather than implying guaranteed conditions.

  3. Prepare a flexible plan

    Consider possible quieter periods, accommodations to ask about, and user-selected preparation strategies. Keep space for a break or a change of plan.

PLANNED CAPABILITIES

The details
we’re exploring.

  • Discover destinations with available sensory-access information.
  • Bring together reports about noise, lighting, and crowd conditions.
  • Create personal sensory preferences and outing plans.
  • Suggest potentially quieter visiting times and accommodations to request.
  • Combine user reports with available environmental information.
  • Offer preparation and calming strategies selected by the person using it.

AN EVERYDAY EXAMPLE

What support could look like.

A museum visit could start with a review of reported sensory conditions, possible quieter periods, and a personal plan for breaks.

A design consideration

Conditions change. Reports would need source and freshness information, with uncertainty made clear. A useful service depends on reliable data and participation.

ACCESSIBILITY & CONTROL

Designed around
the person using it.

Clear comparisons, predictable navigation, readable reports, and control over sensory preferences would be part of the design direction.

Privacy, affordability, and user autonomy are shared Biro.dev design principles. Product-specific data practices, supported access methods, and any offline capabilities would be explained before public release.

Read our design commitments

QUESTIONS ABOUT SENSORYSCOUT

A clearer picture.

Would it measure live conditions everywhere?

No. Reliable location information is a development challenge. Live coverage, specific data sources, and participating venues are still being decided.

Would a sensory-friendly label fit everyone?

No. People experience environments differently. The goal is information matched to individual preferences, rather than a universal rating.

Could families prepare a child for the visit?

Preparation is part of the planned direction. A future optional connection with StoryReady could be useful, but cross-product connections are not available today.

When can I use SensoryScout?

SensoryScout is in early concept development. There is no public release date, price, or supported-platform list yet. The next step is to develop and evaluate the intended experience.
